# ax25-tools

**Configures the kernel AX.25 stack — ports, interfaces, NET/ROM, Rose**

- **Version recorded:** 0.0.10
- **Categories:** `packet-terminals`
- **Upstream:** <https://linux-ax25.in-berlin.de/wiki/Main_Page>
- **Needs from the kernel:** `ax25` — checked against the running kernel at plan time; see [kernel-ax25](../reference/kernel-ax25.md)

## What it does

The administrative half of Linux AX.25: attaches a serial TNC or a KISS device to the kernel stack, brings AX.25 interfaces up, configures NET/ROM and Rose, and runs the daemons that let inbound connections reach a program. It carries kissattach, axparms, mheard, ax25d and the rest.

## Why you would want it

Linux has AX.25 in the kernel, which is unusual and genuinely useful -- packet connections are sockets, so ordinary programs can use them. This is what turns that from a compiled-in capability into a working port.

## Before it will work

A port definition in `/etc/ax25/axports` naming your callsign, the device, and the speed. Hammunition appends one, `wl2k <your callsign> 1200 255 7 Winlink` -- the port pat's AX.25 transport uses by default -- from station config (`hammunition station set --callsign <yours>`). Attaching that port to Direwolf or a TNC with `kissattach` is still yours to do. With no callsign set the package installs and the line is reported as not written.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`packet`](../profiles/packet.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install ax25-tools --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `mheard-stations`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `ax25-tools`

## Configuration it writes

- `/etc/ax25/axports` (appended to, mode 0644, existing file backed up); filled from the station values `ax25_callsign`, and not written while one is unset (D-035)

## Known problems

Linux 7.1 removed the kernel AX.25 stack -- net/ax25, net/netrom, net/rose and every driver in drivers/net/hamradio -- in merge 64edfa65 of 2026-04-24. On a 7.1 or newer kernel there is nothing for kissattach to attach to: `socket(AF_AX25)` fails with "Address family not supported by protocol", and no modprobe helps because the module does not exist. Measured 2026-09-04: Kali rolling (7.1.5) and Pop!_OS 24.04 on its 7.1.5 kernel lack it; Debian 13 (6.12), Parrot 7.3 (7.0.13), Ubuntu 24.04 (6.8) and Ubuntu 26.04 (7.0.0) carry it as a module. Debian removed ax25-tools from testing on 2026-09-01 (#1143282) because it no longer builds against the headers that left with the subsystem, so Kali's archive lacks the package too. Hammunition reads the running kernel's module tree at plan time and refuses this unit by name, or defers it out of a profile, on a kernel without ax25. The userspace packet path is unaffected: Direwolf's KISS and AGW ports serve pat (`ax25+agwpe`), linbpq, YAAC and Xastir without kernel AX.25. See `docs/reference/kernel-ax25.md`. An unconfigured axports produces failures that name a port rather than saying the file is empty, which reads as a hardware problem. The AX.25 stack has a long history of being lightly maintained in the kernel, and some of the more exotic paths -- Rose in particular -- have few users and correspondingly few bug reports. A callsign written into axports is transmitted; it is the station identity, not a label. What the configuration block does: appends the `wl2k` line above to `/etc/ax25/axports` (mode 0644), with a comment line naming it as ours. It is not appended when the file already has a port named `wl2k` or a port on your callsign, because libax25 refuses a second one of either -- so a re-run changes nothing, and a port you defined yourself is left alone. The file as it was is copied first to `/etc/ax25/axports.hammunition-backup`, once. The line is written only when the callsign is an AX.25 address (one to six letters and digits); a callsign such as `W1AW/4` is reported as unusable rather than trimmed. On a kernel without ax25 the unit is refused or deferred, and the line with it. Inspect with `grep -v '^#' /etc/ax25/axports`. `hammunition uninstall ax25-tools` does not remove it (config files are not reversed, and the plan says so); to undo, delete the two `wl2k` lines with `sudoedit /etc/ax25/axports`, or put the backup back with `sudo mv /etc/ax25/axports.hammunition-backup /etc/ax25/axports`.
